Go ahead. Good evening, Mayor and Council. So today
we're here to talk about Kitchener 2051 and specifically evaluating approaches to growth.
So Kitchener 2051 is a project about developing the City's new Official Plan, and determining
the preferred approach to how we grow and change by 2051 is a key component of the new
Official Plan and is shaped by multiple inputs, including the City's current strategic plan,
community values that had emerged over the course of community engagement undertaken
this past fall, big ideas that represent important areas in which we must make significant progress
and focus areas that help identify how to achieve them, and the ways in which we can
evaluate approaches to growth, which is what we're here to talk about today.
All these inputs will lead to Official Plan policies that will ultimately implement this
vision for Kitchener in 2051.
The Kitchener 2051 project team engaged with over 2,000 residents and collaborators during
our Phase II engagement program this past fall.
Working with our engagement consultant team, we have distilled five community values which
represent the broad themes of what we heard over the course of the engagement and serve
as a bridge between the engagement and future technical work.
As we move forward with our technical and engagement processes, these values will be
reflected in emerging policy directions and will ultimately shape the new official plan.
As I just mentioned a couple of slides ago, the big ideas represent the areas in which
the new Official Plan must make significant progress and touch on the themes of our neighbourhoods,
our economy and our environment.
We also have focus areas that identify tangible and more specific ways in which these big
ideas can be achieved.
The big ideas, along with the focus areas and community values, were previously presented
at a Council strategic session held this past February 10th.
So the Kitchener 2051 project is now at the point where we will be assessing where and
how Kitchener can grow and change by 2051.
This assessment will be informed by three components, community parameters, technical
evaluation criteria, and Council direction and cross-divisional staff priorities.
The evaluation process is anticipated to result in a preferred approach to growth that reflects
a composite or hybrid of all three of the approaches and refined based off of the evaluation process.
The first of these inputs include community parameters, which were informed by the community
values and vetted by the Kitchener 2051 Community Working Group.
The community parameters will help facilitate conversations with the community about trade-offs,
and opportunities about how and where Kitchener can grow in the future.
These parameters are not intended to be exhaustive or lead someone toward picking a preferred approach.
Rather, they will focus on understanding the community's priorities that will ultimately inform a preferred hybrid composite scenario.
The second input includes technical evaluation criteria.
These are informed by the Kitchener 2051 technical studies and modelling work.
They include criteria to assess physical infrastructure, including the ability of Kitchener's roads and underground pipes to accommodate potential growth and change.
These criteria will enable analysis of each approach to growth and identify different opportunities and constraints that may need to be addressed.
They're also broken down into five distinct themes.
Supporting Kitchener's economy.
Protecting and enhancing the natural heritage system.
being future-focused, planning for change across the city, and planning for greater
integration of places, systems, and networks. Additional information on these technical
criteria are included as part of Attachment A to the staff report.
The third input into setting the approaches to growth include Council direction and cross-divisional
staff priorities, which are informed by regular and ongoing engagement with yourselves, along
with City staff. In terms of next steps related to the evaluation of approaches to growth,
we will be hosting an engagement event and speaker series on Saturday, April 5 at St.
Mary's High School. With the engagement, we'll continue throughout April with the use of
the community conversation kit that will see conversations facilitated by the community
with community members on emerging policy directions that could ultimately find their
way into the new Official Plan.
Additional information and a digital version of the in-person engagement events will be
available on the project webpage at engagewr.ca slash kitchener2051.
This upcoming round of engagement in April accompanies ongoing dialogue with First Nations
and Kitchener 2051's community working group.
In conclusion, staff are recommending that the community parameters and technical evaluation
criteria as presented in report DSD 2025-084 be used to inform continued community and
collaborator engagement on KITRIN 2051 and approaches to growth.
